deterministic_bounds.scope: These finite historical rows only, no generalization estimate or confidence interval.

interpretation: Recovered C and D exactly implement the observable first-record output rule on all 32 saved distant update rows, across both counterfactuals and templates. Near rows have three C and two D counterexamples, so this is not an unconditional deterministic all-position rule.

The old TRAIN update targets are first-record-biased (24/32 rows, 6/8 worlds), not always first. Old DEV correct revisions are first only 12/64 rows (3/16 worlds). Positional shortcut reward differs across these registered splits.
Original-architecture B also shifts strongly toward first-record outputs (59/64 overall), so added recurrence is unnecessary for this historical adaptation-associated pattern.

Fixed whole-output literal decoding isolates formatting: source A has 18 literal-correct update rows versus 14 strict-correct; adapted B/C have 13 under both and D12. Aggregate matrix gains elsewhere do not imply improved revision selection.

Within the matched old A/B/C/D matrix, exposure and delta bindings support a descriptive adaptation-associated output shift. No stage-specific behavioral outputs, TRAIN model predictions or order-balanced control are saved, so learning mechanism and which training phase caused the shift remain unisolated.

Counterfactual replacements alter only the correct event value while preserving order/revisions. Distant C/D predictions therefore change in only the three worlds whose correct revision is first, and remain unchanged in the other thirteen target-changing worlds.
Rule agreement can overlap: first-record, largest-code and largest-revision may select the same literal. Rank fits describe outputs and cannot reveal an exclusive internal algorithm.
No comparison to the new anchor is made. Old template/geometry differences and a different corpus cannot support a cross-corpus causal gain/loss claim.
limitations: One source, site, seed and old synthetic DEV corpus; exploratory pattern inspection, no confirmation evidence or promotion/gain claim.
The 64 DEV update rows are 16 dependent worlds with four variants each, not 64 independent samples.
Only saved predictions are analyzed; no native model reexecution, numerical delta payload interpretation or GPU workload.
No TRAIN predictions are saved: TRAIN analysis concerns stimulus/target ordering and known update exposure only.
Literal decoding is a newly explicit descriptive audit of old output strings and does not replace registered strict metrics.
No cross-corpus causal inference with any new anchor; no automatic longer context, recurrence campaign or recovery training.
literal_decoder_contract:
Parse one complete JSON value: {'v': decimal string/int}, decimal string/int.

    No prose extraction, substring matching, fences, booleans, floats, null,
    additional keys or numeric revision/code rewriting. Decimal strings preserve
    exact text; integers convert by ordinary decimal str().

minimal_actionable_intervention_not_an_e.balanced_recovery_intervention_if_separa: Counterbalance correct-revision position and numeric code ranking within equal world/exposure budgets, with a matched original-order training control and fixed held-out permutation worlds. Exact record-order change is the isolated intervention; keep source, tokenizer, optimizer, precision, site, steps and total exposure fixed.
minimal_actionable_intervention_not_an_e.current_decision: Offline evidence only. No native retry, new corpus, new grant, training, evaluation, source edit or run proposal is created by this audit. RAM guard remains a stopping condition.
minimal_actionable_intervention_not_an_e.mechanistic_hypothesis: The old recovery distribution rewards a first-record shortcut more often than genuine revision comparison, and adaptation increases use of that shortcut on unseen templates.
minimal_actionable_intervention_not_an_e.minimum_interpretation: A changed output following the new first event while the oracle target stays fixed supports a positional-output dependence at those rows; it does not by itself show an internal learned algorithm or broad capability change.
minimal_actionable_intervention_not_an_e.prospective_analysis: Separate greatest-revision literal correctness, first/last/largest-code agreement, target-changing counterfactual response, source-correct damage and formatting; group dependent variants by world.
minimal_actionable_intervention_not_an_e.smallest_behavioral_control: Hold subject, three distinct code values, three distinct revisions, query, filler and oracle target constant; change only evidence record order so the same greatest-revision event moves from first to a later slot. Choose values so greatest code and greatest revision are different events. Compare first-record and true-rule literal predictions, preserving strict output metrics separately.
